articles.title: AFC North Predictions: Who Takes The Steelers Spot As The Top AFC North Team?
articles.summary: The "First Things First" co-hosts made their AFC North predictions on Wednesday's edition of the show.
articles.body: The Steelers reign as the AFC North title winners, but two teams are emerging as stronger candidates to win one of the most competitive divisions in football this season, at least according to "First Things First." From the questions surrounding the Pittsburgh Steelers' Aaron Rodgers and the Cleveland Browns' Deshaun Watson, and the healthy talent returning on both the Baltimore Ravens' and Cincinnati Bengals' rosters, the AFC North seems to be unpredictable this season. However, Nick Wright, Chris Broussard and Danny Parkins were in unison on who the top two teams in the division will be. Here are their picks for the AFC North. Nick Wright's AFC North Prediction 1.Baltimore Ravens 2.Cincinnati Bengals 3.Pittsburgh Steelers 4.Cleveland Browns Nick Wright put the Cleveland Browns at the bottom and the Ravens at the top, leaving last year's AFC North winners at third. Wright did not hold back when it came to the Browns, emphasizing that its quarterback situation does not benefit them or its record. "I think they’re going to be 4-13. I think it’s the worst quarterback situation in the NFL. … I’d be very surprised if they win six games," Wright said on Wednesday's edition of First Things First. In terms of the Steelers, the return of Rodgers could go South for new head coach Mike McCarthy, especially with Rodgers turning 43 years old this year. "I think they finish 6-11, but what is Aaron Rodgers going to look like once the weather turns cold? … He turns 43 this year," Wright said. "I would be surprised if, during that stretch that Drew Allar doesn't start a game or two … I do not think Aaron Rodgers will be the starting quarterback all year." Wright believes that Cincinnati will fall into the same cycle as last year: win nine games and miss the playoffs. Even with quarterback Joe Burrow back in full force with wide receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, Wright is not buying any of the hype surrounding its offense. "Winning only nine games and missing the playoffs. It’s basically what they do every year… I think they will have the ninth-best offense in the NFL." For Wright's No. 1 team, the Ravens, he sets the bar high for quarterback Lamar Jackson and new head coach Jesse Minter. Wright predicts that Baltimore will also land the No. 1 seed in the AFC. "I would be shocked if they don’t start 6-0. If they don’t just sweep this conference. I am predicting that the Baltimore Ravens will be the No. 1 seed in the AFC," Wright continued. "I think Minter is a breath of fresh air this year. I think Lamar might win his third NFL MVP. They might be a regular season juggernaut." Chris Broussard's AFC North Prediction 1.Baltimore Ravens 2.Cincinnati Bengals 3.Pittsburgh Steelers 4.Cleveland Browns Chris Broussard and Wright shared the same predictions from top to bottom. However, there's a twist that came with the Bengals. For Broussard, the Browns were the clear choice for fourth place, especially with their offseason decision on starting quarterback Deshaun Watson. "I’m stunned that Deshaun Watson has won the job. He hasn’t played well… He better go out and win those first two road games," Broussard said. Broussard also turned heads when he made his prediction about the Steelers season, noting it could be their first losing season in over two decades. "This will be the first losing season for the Steelers since 2003. We’re going to find out that Mike Tomlin was really holding that thing together…I think Mike McCarthy is a good coach, but the last two years he was with Aaron Rodgers in Green Bay…they went 8-10-1…with a team that had the potential to win 13 games," Broussard said. Rodgers left every NFL fan waiting for his offseason decision to return to Pittsburgh, retire or sign with someone new. However, joining forces with McCarthy adds a new element to the Steelers' success this season. Broussard's prediction for the Bengals is that they do make the playoffs, but won't win the division. "They get to the playoffs. I’m expecting a nice year from them, I’m expecting Burrow to be healthy," Broussard said. "The defense is just going to be solid… I think the offense is going to be one of the best in the league." And none other than Broussard's favorite NFL team, the Ravens, took place as the AFC North winners. "I am EXCITED about this season," Broussard said. Danny Parkins' AFC North Prediction 1.Cincinnati Bengals 2.Baltimore Ravens 3.Pittsburgh Steelers 4.Cleveland Browns Parkins followed suit with the Browns in last place, thanks to their lack of talent at quarterback. "Very obvious. They’re going to play three quarterbacks this season… They’re going to move to Shedeur Sanders early, and then they’re going to have no other move, and they’ll be in trouble," Parkins said. "I think that they’re one quarterback away from making things interesting." The Steelers placed third, noting that their regular season ended with eight wins and Rodgers will be ‘fine’ this season. "I think they’re going to be fine. I think Aaron Rodgers is going to go out with a whimper, they’ll be an eight-win team," Parkins said. However, Parkins split off from Broussard and Wright's predictions and placed the Ravens second, but still making the playoffs. Parkins detailed that Minter could be a good hire on paper, but won't know much until the season rolls around. "I think it’s going to take 12 wins to win this division. … My thing with Baltimore is, I think Jesse Minter is a good hire, but we don’t know," Parkins said. "We have a head coach who’s never been a head coach, you have an offensive coordinator who’s never been a playcaller." Parkins labeled the Bengals as his team to win the division. However, even with the talented offense Cincinnati has, the Bengals top the Ravens by a very small amount. "As for Cincinnati, when Joe Burrow, Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase play, they’re 12-6 over the last two seasons and averaging 29 points per game, and they added a ton to their defense. So, on the thinnest of margins, I have the Bengals over the Ravens," Parkins said.

articles.title: Alberto Gamero habría llegado a un acuerdo para regresar a Millonarios
articles.summary: Tras la sorpresiva salida del entrenador argentino Fabián Bustos del banquillo de Millonarios, las directivas del conjunto 'embajador' se movieron con rapidez para encontrar a su sustituto. La búsqueda apuntó de manera directa a un viejo conocido de la casa: Alberto Gamero, quien habría llegado a un acuerdo total para iniciar su segunda etapa al frente del equipo capitalino.
articles.body: Tras la sorpresiva salida del entrenador argentino Fabián Bustos del banquillo de Millonarios, las directivas del conjunto 'embajador' se movieron con rapidez para encontrar a su sustituto. La búsqueda apuntó de manera directa a un viejo conocido de la casa: Alberto Gamero, quien habría llegado a un acuerdo total para iniciar su segunda etapa al frente del equipo capitalino. De acuerdo con la información divulgada por varios medios, las conversaciones entre los altos mandos del club, con el visto bueno del director deportivo Ariel Michaloutsos, y el entrenador samario llegaron a un puerto próspero. Tras sostener reuniones clave en Bogotá, se logró un principio de acuerdo para formalizar el inicio de una nueva etapa de Gamero en el banquillo embajador. Luego de que se hiciera oficial la desvinculación de Bustos, el gerente deportivo Ariel Michaloutsos y la cúpula dirigencial de Millonarios definieron como prioridad absoluta el retorno del estratega samario. Gamero, quien se encontraba libre tras finalizar su vínculo previo con Deportivo Cali y venía realizando actividades académicas en Panamá junto a Radamel Falcao García, interrumpió su agenda para reunirse en Bogotá con la cúpula directiva. Pese a contar con el interés de otros clubes de la Liga Colombiana —entre ellos Junior de Barranquilla—, el peso afectivo e histórico del proyecto 'embajador' inclinó la balanza de manera definitiva. Alberto Gamero dejó una huella marcada en su primer paso por Millonarios entre 2020 y 2024. Durante sus cinco temporadas construyó un proceso caracterizado por la consolidación de canteranos y un estilo de juego definido que se tradujo en tres títulos oficiales para la vitrina albiazul: Su salida a finales de 2024 se produjo en términos institucionales cordiales debido a un desgaste natural tras un largo ciclo. Sin embargo, la inestabilidad del banquillo en los meses posteriores llevó a la dirigencia a apostar de nuevo por la fórmula que le brindó identidad y resultados. Mientras se ultiman los detalles del contrato y la presentación oficial del nuevo cuerpo técnico, el equipo afronta sus compromisos inmediatos bajo el mando interino de los profesores Omar Rodríguez y Guiam Carlos Espinoza. Se prevé que el estratega de 62 años asuma formalmente los entrenamientos en los próximos días para reorientar al plantel en la recta en desarrollo del torneo. Su debut oficial en el banquillo en este nuevo ciclo está previsto para la fecha 9 del campeonato, en el duelo donde Millonarios visitará al Deportivo Pereira. El entrenador samario asume el proyecto con metas sumamente exigentes para el remate de la temporada: Con el acuerdo cerrado y la expectativa en lo más alto, la hinchada de Millonarios aguarda la oficialización y presentación del entrenador para dar inicio al segundo capítulo de Alberto Gamero en Bogotá.

articles.title: Why did Brad Marchand aim at Tim Stützle during Ottawa Senators’ NHL leadership discussions
articles.summary: NHL News: Florida Panthers forward Brad Marchand mocks Tim Stützle during the Ottawa Senators' search for a new captain, igniting debate over the team's leadership choices.
articles.body: The search for a new captain for the Ottawa Senators has caught the attention of NHL teams, and Florida Panthers forward Brad Marchand has emerged as an unlikely name in the mix. Marchand posted on Instagram regarding Ottawa’s reported captaincy finalists and made a mocking comment about Tim Stützle.The comment came after the Ottawa Senators lost Brady Tkachuk, who was traded to the Florida Panthers on June 21 for four draft picks. Tim Stützle, Jake Sanderson and Thomas Chabot are said to be on the organization's radar for the role, with the captaincy now open. did Brad Marchand mock Tim Stützle and Ottawa Senators? Brad Marchand took a shot at Tim Stützle in reaction to an internet debate over the Ottawa Senators’ captaincy race, without explaining why he said it.A Senators leadership situation was highlighted on an Instagram account, Puckempire. Marchand shot back with a short message, laughing at the idea of Stützle being the next captain in Ottawa. The Florida Panthers forward didn’t offer any additional context or criticism with the comment.The reaction came after it was reported that Tim Stützle, Jake Sanderson and Thomas Chabot are the three frontrunners for the Ottawa Senators captaincy.Since arriving in the NHL, Stützle has become one of Ottawa’s most important offensive weapons. The 24-year-old center has also taken on a larger role within the team and sported an alternate captain’s “A” for stretches last season.That makes Marchand’s comment notable, but not the position of the Ottawa Senators organization. The captaincy decision is an internal matter that Ottawa Senators president of hockey operations Steve Staios and head coach Travis Green are expected to weigh in on.Tim Stützle is among the candidates for the vacant Ottawa Senators captaincy as his role continues to grow.The German-born center is a key part of Ottawa’s long-term plans. His growth as a more complete two-way player has only strengthened his case for more leadership responsibility.Jake Sanderson has a strong case as well because of his role on the blue line in Ottawa, but Thomas Chabot has much more experience and is the longest-serving Senator of the reported finalists.Now, Brad Marchand is a teammate of former Senators captain Brady Tkachuk with the Florida Panthers, so the veteran forward has a direct connection to the player who left to create the vacancy.Throughout his NHL career, Marchand has also been known for his abrasive comments and aggressive personality on and off the ice. The Stützle remark is consistent with the style that has followed him throughout his career, given his history of trying to get under opponents' skin.Who could become the next Ottawa Senators captain?The Ottawa Senators have yet to publicly call for a captain, with Tim Stützle, Jake Sanderson and Thomas Chabot reported as the frontrunners.The choice will be the 10th captain in franchise history. Marchand’s social media comment has sparked debate, but it’s expected to come down to Ottawa’s assessment of leadership, character, experience and long-term value to the franchise.Right now, the NHL conversation surrounding the Senators’ captaincy is focused on the three internal candidates rather than outside commentary. Marchand’s jab has added a little more attention to the debate, but it doesn’t change the decision Ottawa’s management faces.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘I am so sorry’: Former NFL star dies tragically after concerning Facebook post
articles.summary: The NFL world is in mourning just days before the start of the 2026 season as former NFL star Alphonso Smith Jr. has tragically died at the age of 40 after a...
articles.body:
The NFL world is in mourning just days before the start of the 2026 season as former NFL star Alphonso Smith Jr. has tragically died at the age of 40 after a concerning post on Facebook.

The news comes after Smith made a Facebook post in which he referred to himself as a "coward" and said he is "so sorry."

Smith emerged as a star cornerback for the Wake Forest Demon Deacons, where he played from 2004 to 2008.

During his senior season at Wake Forest, he started all 13 games and emerged as one of the top corners in the country, earning consensus All-American honors. He was also one of five finalists for the Bronko Nagurski Trophy and continues to hold the ACC record for interceptions in a career with 21.

Following his standout college football career, Smith was selected with the No. 37 overall pick by the Denver Broncos. After spending the 2009 season with the Broncos, he was traded to the Detroit Lions, where he played from 2010 to 2012 when his football career came to an end.

According to a report from TMZ Sports , Smith took his own life at a housing community in Florida after posting a concerning message on Facebook.

"Do not cry for me! I tried everything in my power to fight the demons behind the ones that someone put into ME! I did not want to be that WAY! I know I have disappointed so many folks. This is a DEMON in me! But not only me! It's EVERYONE! I have HURT so many! I needed help & did not get it! I am so sorry! I am a piece of sh*t! It's a lot of you that are! I am A COWARD! A HUGE COWARD! I am so sorry…

"To my kids, daddy is SO SORRY! To my friends, I love you all, but your boy was f*cked up! To my family, BABY, my MOM, my siblings, things happened to your boy, your brother while I was little that an older lady did onto me. As a result guys, I did the same onto others! Please forgive me!

"Please pray over your families! PLEASE PRAY FOR ALL I've affected! I am the WORST & I pray my soul rest in heaven for my heart is pure, but my BRAIN & experience is MESSED UP!!"

Smith ended his letter with "I'm SORRY! THIS IS IT!"

articles.title: Marc Marquez given brutal warning ahead of Pedro Acosta Ducati showdown
articles.summary: Marc Marquez could be facing the toughest task of his career when he faces up against Pedro Acosta at Ducati next season. That’s according to his former titl...
articles.body:
Marc Marquez could be facing the toughest task of his career when he faces up against Pedro Acosta at Ducati next season.

That's according to his former title rival, Andrea Dovizioso, who sees the pairing as unlike anything Marquez has experienced before .

The nine-time champion will be joined in Italy by Acosta next season after the pair signed contracts with Ducati for 2027 and 2028.

Acosta is yet to win a MotoGP race, but is a champion in Moto2 and Moto3, and has thrilled ever since he stepped up to the premier class with KTM.

The deal has whetted the appetites of many, and also provoked some to question whether it could signal that Marquez's legendary career is coming to an end.

Acosta and Marquez are all smiles now, but that could change next season (Credit: Red Bull Content Pool)

It's also prompted comparisons to when Valentino Rossi was joined by Jorge Lorenzo at Yamaha in 2008, creating a two-pronged attack of elite riders and an almighty rivalry.

However, Dovizioso has explained why the analogy isn't quite right.

Marc Marquez and Acosta pairing compared to Rossi vs Lorenzo

"Marc isn't in the same situation as Valentino. Valentino, however, was still at the top," he said on the podcast 04 bar.

"Yes, he wasn't so young anymore, but he'd been there for many years. Marc isn't in that situation; physically, he has too many problems."

Marquez prompted retirement fears earlier this season when he fractured his ankle at Le Mans and was caught in tears as he explained the pain in his shoulder.

A double surgery has eased the pain, but the 33-year-old has been to hell and back with arm issues, going through seven operations since 2020 and missing numerous races.

Dovizioso thinks it's clear he can no longer race at his peak, nor hide those struggles from his rivals.

Dovizioso says Marquez can no longer hide physical limitations

He explained: "He's not just upset, he's desperate.

"Now he's not hiding it anymore, because, after all, he's a strategist and he's tried to downplay his limitations while he could, but they were so obvious that now they're plain for all to see.

"As a strategist, why show an expression of total exhaustion after a race where you suffered a lot and had no control over your body? He said that.

"It's the worst thing you can tell your rival, but that expression, when he describes those sensations, you see there's nothing [left] to interpret..."

It's not just Marquez's physical limitations, though, but Acosta's talent that has Dovizioso questioning how things will play out at Ducati next season.

Last time out in Aragon, Marquez won the race , but Acosta followed him home in second on a KTM whose development has been halted as the manufacturer instead focuses on the 2027 regulation changes.

Dovizioso intrigued by 'real Acosta' at Ducati

"In my opinion, there's still a lot to discover about Acosta in many aspects, despite all the extraordinary things he's already done. Both in terms of his character and his behaviour," Dovizioso said.

"We don't know him very well because he's young and he's going to change teams; it's the first time he's racing a different bike with a specific team, as Marc's teammate.

"It will be an interesting situation and we'll soon start to discover the real Acosta. Right now it's a little difficult."

articles.title: 2026 Week 1 Preview: Oregon State Beavers @ Houston Cougars
articles.summary: Houston and Oregon State open on ESPN in a rematch of a 2025 Friday night thriller.
articles.body:
Time and date: Saturday, September 5 at 12:00 p.m. ET

Last meeting: Houston 27, Oregon State 24 — September 26, 2025

A different energy resonates throughout the air in Houston, TX.

For the first time since joining the Big 12, the Houston Cougars enter a season with expectations. Ranked No. 23 in the AP Poll, they enter with their highest preseason ranking since 2016. Fresh off a 10-win season, the Cougars retained head coach Willie Fritz, all three coordinators, and many of last year's top contributors. Fritz orchestrated a rapid rise from the cellar of the Big 12, and now the pieces are in place for conference championship contention.

Oregon State hopes to engineer a similar turnaround in Corvallis. The Beavers enjoyed considerable success in the early 2020s, but the program took a dramatic step backward when the classic iteration Pac-12 dissolved. After stumbling to 2-10 in 2025, Oregon State replaced head coach Trent Bray with JaMarcus Shephard, who hopes to make the Beavers a force in the revamped Pac-12.

Despite the stark contrast between their 2-10 and 10-3 records, the Beavers nearly stunned the Cougars in 2025. Houston stormed back down 14 in the final seven minutes and blocked Oregon State field goal at the buzzer to force overtime. Upon reaching the extra frame, the Cougars escaped on a walk-off field goal.

This year the series shifts to Houston, where Fritz's team enters as a significant favorite in a nationally televised showcase.

Oregon State opened the 2023 season ranked No. 18 in the AP Poll. Three years later, the program is coming off a dismal 2-10 record. The Beavers weren't as bad as their record suggested, at least during the first half of 2025. They led 9-4 Fresno State with under one minute remaining and held a 14-point fourth quarter advantage over 10-3 Houston. But the 0-7 start ultimately proved too much to overcome, as the Beavers slipped up against the likes of Tulsa and Sam Houston late in the season. Now JaMarcus Shephard aims to restore order.

One of Shephard's first major decisions involved selecting a starting quarterback. Rather than stick with incumbent Maalik Murphy, who served as Duke's starter in 2024, Shephard appointed Mercer transfer Braden Atkinson to QB1. Atkinson finished second in the FCS with 3,611 passing yards last fall, delivering 34 touchdowns against 11 interceptions on a 65.8 completion rate. He'll be tasked with improving the efficiency of a passing attack that completed only 14 touchdown passes, while tossing 13 interceptions in 2025.

Atkinson's supporting cast will look considerably different from Murphy's last year. Oregon State loses each of its top four leading receivers, and tight end Gabe Milbourn (17 receptions, 185 yards) and wide receiver Eddie Freauff (12 receptions, 144 yards) are the returning leaders in production. The Beavers turned to the portal for reinforcements, landing former Texas State receivers Aaron Butler and Xayvion Noland and Alabama transfer Aeryn Hampton, who followed new offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen from Tuscaloosa. True freshman Jesse Legree and former Central Michigan tight end DeCorion Temple could also play significant roles in an offense that ranked 18th nationally in passing attempts per game last fall.

The Beavers produced the 125th ranked scoring offense at 18.2 points per game, but one of their few bright spots was 1,000-yard rusher Anthony Hankerson. While Hankerson is gone, Oregon State can lean on Cornell Hatcher Jr., who turned in his best performance against Houston last season with 93 rushing yards and a touchdown. Vanderbilt transfer AJ Newberry also joins a running back room which possesses plenty of size. They'll run behind an offensive line returning three starters from the Trent Bray era.

Oregon State's defense played particularly well against Houston last September, but the unit lacked consistency throughout the season, allowing over 30 points in seven of 12 contests. This year's unit will operate under the direction of Mike MacIntyre, who previously served as head coach of FIU and Colorado. Despite the coaching turnover, the Beavers still retain five primary starters from 2025, headlined by middle linebacker Aiden Sullivan, the team's second-leading tackler and tackles for loss leader.

MacIntyre's defense should be strongest in the secondary. The Beavers held opposing quarterbacks to a 56.9 completion percentage a year ago and bring back cornerback Trey Glasper and nickel Sai Vadrawale, who combined for 54 tackles, 10 pass deflections, and two interceptions. TJ Crandall, who fractured his foot during fall camp last August, returns after previously last playing at West Virginia in 2024.

Forcing turnovers was a struggle for Oregon State in 2025. Sullivan forced three fumbles, but the team only recovered one all season. The Beavers finished a minus-11 in the turnover battle last year, but a plus-1 margin against Houston played a massive role in the near upset.

Houston won't sneak up on anybody this year. Opponents are well aware of the Cougars' capabilities after last sesaon's 10-3 finish. Last season, Houston was the only team to finish 6-0 on the road, yet comparatively struggled at home with a 3-3 record. The Cougars emerged victorious in six of seven one-score games, hoping that statistic proves sustainable, rather than an anomaly that could regress to the mean.

Returning an established starting quarterback is always a plus, and Houston has that in Conner Weigman. In his first year as a Cougar, the former 5-star Texas A&M recruit produced 2,705 yards, 25 touchdowns, and nine interceptions. However, the reigning Texas Bowl MVP — who regularly dealt with lower-body injuries at his previous stop — surprised many defenses with his mobility. Weigman eclipsed 80 rushing yards in six games, including three outings with at least 110. Although Houston landed the No. 1 quarterback recruit in the country in Keisean Henderson this offseason, Weigman retains his starting duties as a fifth-year senior.

Houston's offense also returns Amare Thomas. The First Team All-Big 12 wide receiver is the conference's returning leader in receiving yards (966) and touchdowns (12). Thomas dominated the production at the position in 2025, as no other Cougar wide receiver recorded more than 13 catches or 275 yards. The group should be deeper this year thanks to the combined development of Koby Young and Harvey Broussard, and the arrivals of transfers Tyson Turner (Texas Tech) and Trent Walker (Oregon State). Saturday will be an emotional game for Walker, who faces his former team after producing consecutive 800+ yard seasons in Corvallis.

The Cougars lose a near-1,000-yard rusher in Dean Connors but reload with Makhi Hughes, who surpassed 1,300 yards in consecutive seasons at Tulane. The former Green Wave star reunites with Willie Fritz, although he eyes a bounce-back season after being underutilized at Oregon in 2025. Hughes will be supported by his former star guard Shadre Hurst. One of the most coveted portal additions this offseason, Hurst arrives as an AP First Team Preseason All-American selection, while boasting some of the most impressive weight-room numbers among FBS linemen. Two former All-MAC stars — center Anthony Boswell and right tackle Drew Terrill — also join a restructured Houston line that ranked in the top 30 in fewest sacks allowed last year.

Houston fielded a solid defense overall in coordinator Austin Armstrong's first year at the helm. Now Armstrong's unit enters 2026 with a healthy mix of returning talent and transfers. While the Cougars lose tackles leader Carlos Allen and sacks leader Eddie Walls on the defensive line, they replace them with substantially more size. Ashton Porter arrives from Oregon as a 6'3", 280-pound defensive end, while defensive tackles Ejiro Egodogbare (6'3", 310) and De'Marion Thomas (6'2", 340) bolster the interior. The front also returns contributors such as Khalil Laufau, who dominated in the Texas Bowl last December, and Brandon Mack II, the team's returning sacks leader with 5.0.

The linebacking corps retains Sione Fotu and adds transfer Jaden Yates, a former First Team All-Sun Belt selection at Marshall who started nine games for a College Football Playoff-caliber Ole Miss team. The secondary offers more continuity, retaining All-Big 12 cornerback Will James and both starting safeties, Kentrell Webb and Jordan Allen. James recorded a team-high three interceptions and broke up eight passes as a sophomore last year, and he'll be supported by new transfers. Jalen Mayo, an FCS All-American cornerback who transferred from Stephen F. Austin, occupies the other boundary corner, while Tulane transfer Javion White takes over as the nickel.

According to ESPN, Oregon State had a 99.3 percent chance of winning when Houston faced a 3rd and 17 with 6:49 remaining in last year's contest. But the Cougars staged a dramatic comeback and now enter as three-touchdown home favorites over the Beavers.

Although Houston was better on the road last season, a home opener against Oregon State should be far more manageable than last September's Friday night road trip to Corvallis. The Cougars might need time to find their offensive rhythm, as they did in Fritz's previous home openers and throughout much of their 10-3 campaign. But thanks to the advantage of their new-look offensive line, they will eventually settle in and rely on star talents like Makhi Hughes and Amare Thomas to sustain drives.

Braden Atkinson has played FBS competition before, throwing for 210 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions against Auburn last November. How he adapts in this offense, surrounded by an unproven but promising group of receivers, is the true wild card in this game.

Oregon State keeps the game competitive in the first half, but Conner Weigman and the Cougars pull away with a two-touchdown victory.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton pays homage to Michael Schumacher ahead of Ferrari’s Monza tribute
articles.summary: The Scuderia will sport a unique Schumacher-related livery on their car at their home event this weekend
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton paid homage to Michael Schumacher ahead of an Italian Grand Prix weekend where Ferrari will adorn a special livery in tribute to the F1 legend.

Joining the team 30 years ago, Schumacher won five of his seven world championships at Ferrari and the prancing horse outfit announced plans earlier this week to dedicate their cars and race suits to the German legend.

The cars of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will sport a livery inspired by the 1996 Ferrari F310, which the German drove in his debut year, and will feature hints of gold on the wheels similar to the '96 model.

The car will also feature Schumacher's logo and the seven stars that used to adorn his helmet, signifying his seven titles – a feat matched only by Hamilton. Ex-Ferrari driver Sebastian Vettel will also drive Schumacher's championship-winning 2022 car for a "celebratory" lap before Sunday's grand prix.

Asked about representing Ferrari at Monza for the second time, Hamilton said in a press conference on Thursday: "It is the best feeling, such an honour and a privilege to be a Ferrari driver. It is really phenomenal to experience it for the second year in a row."

"I haven't seen the [Schumacher] livery yet, but those seven stars that we will have, like mine, give me a good feeling."

"I always remember seeing Michael in the red car, and just trying to imagine what it would feel like to be in his shoes. He was such a leader."

While championship leader Kimi Antonelli will take a grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation and is set to start at the back of the grid, Ferrari have brought a power unit upgrade for round 13.

"Every little helps," said Hamilton, who won his first race for Ferrari in Barcelona in June. "Even the last race, we were losing four tenths on the straight. I'm really proud of how hard everyone is working, in the factory, heads down."

"This is a step forward. It is not the whole gap we need, we knew that would be the case but just to see things coming to the car, it is exciting to see we are still pushing."

Hamilton drove into the Monza paddock on Thursday in his own recently acquired F40 car, emblazoned with his own personal number plate and, seemingly by coincidence, a "number 44 engine."

"I've been looking for one for a while, and I wanted one with low mileage," he explained. "I wanted one with a story, and lots have come up in auction over the past couple of years.

"When they took the engine out, they found out the engine's number 44, it's got stamped on the engine, number 44, I couldn't believe it.

"It feels very much fate and I thought it was a real opportunity to kind of highlight the history of Ferrari in their home country, at their race, and when am I ever going to get to do that again?"

articles.title: Ravens practice squad: Five players who could become contributors
articles.summary: Five young players on the Ravens' practice squad have the traits to become future contributors
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens retained several young players on their practice squad who could eventually compete for active-roster roles. Baltimore's roster is elite and built to win now, leaving limited opportunities for developmental prospects. The practice squad allows those players to improve without requiring the Ravens to sacrifice experienced depth on the 53-man roster.

Here are five prospects with the best long-term potential.

Isaac remains an intriguing pass-rushing prospect despite failing to secure an active-roster position entering his third season. Baltimore selected the former Penn State defender in the third round of the 2024 NFL draft. Injuries disrupted the beginning of his career and prevented him from establishing a consistent role.

The Ravens have significant depth on the edge, but that room could change quickly as contracts expire and veteran players age. Isaac still has an opportunity to develop into a rotational pass rusher if he remains healthy and translates his athleticism into consistent production.

Rucker has the power and physical playing style to develop into a dependable edge-setting defender. He spent the summer competing in one of Baltimore's deepest position groups. The practice squad gives Rucker additional time to expand his pass-rushing bag and improve his work on special teams. Those improvements could make him a candidate for a larger role in 2027.

Baltimore selected Benny in the seventh round before waiving him during final roster reductions. Bringing him back showed the Ravens remain interested in his development. The former Michigan defender has the size to play multiple positions along the defensive front. Learning behind Nnamdi Madubuike, Calais Campbell, Travis Jones and Broderick Washington could help Benny become more technically consistent.

At 6-foot-8 and 330 pounds, Lichtenhan has the frame NFL teams want from an offensive tackle. He also has experience in Baltimore's system after spending time with the organization in 2025. The practice squad will allow him to continue improving his balance, footwork, and hand placement. Offensive tackle is a premium position, making his development particularly valuable.

Dawkins joined the Ravens as an undrafted rookie after starting extensively at Penn State. His intelligence, toughness, and familiarity with making protection calls give Baltimore a natural developmental center. The season-ending injury to Danny Pinter demonstrated how quickly offensive line depth can disappear. Dawkins can use his rookie season to add strength and learn behind Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn.

If he progresses, Dawkins could eventually compete for an interior reserve position that provides depth at center and guard.

articles.title: Who are the three best starting pitchers on the Red Sox right now?
articles.summary: Or perhaps even more importantly, who will the three best starting pitching options be for the Red Sox be on September 29th?
articles.body:
Here at Over The Monster, we like to ask a topical question of the day; but on this dreary morning, we might as well be asking the question of the month. Very simply: If the Wild Card series started today, who would you want starting those three games?

Of course, the Wild Card series doesn't start today, and Red Sox haven't officially punched their ticket into the dance yet. But with FanGraphs giving them a 97.1 percent chance to make the playoffs and only 0.3 percent chance to win the division as of this morning , it seems pretty darn likely they're going to be playing baseball on September 29th (and playing it somewhere other than Fenway Park).

The Red Sox know this as well and have already reshuffled their rotation to pitch Sonny Gray on Saturday (September 5th) and Payton Tolle on Sunday (September 6th). With off days for the month already scheduled for the 10th, 14th, 17th, and 28th (assuming they make the playoffs), this means Gray and Tolle could pitch with an extra day of rest every start from here to the end of the year in a normal five man rotation and be perfectly lined up to pitch Game 1 and Game 2 of the Wild Card series. (September 11th and 12th against the Royals, September 17th and 18th against the Rangers and Rays, September 23rd and 24th against the Guardians, and September 29th and 30th against the Wild Card opponent.)

So the Red Sox have already told us who they believe will start the first two games of the playoffs indirectly, but third option is far more complex. Historically, Ranger Suarez would be the best man for the job. Not only did they just give him a $130 million contract in January, but he also has a 1.48 career ERA in the playoffs. However, the Sox might not be too pleased with the way he threw the ball in Sunday's start against the Yankees with the tiebreaker on the line, and they might not want to set things up that way again for a potential winner take all game on October 1st.

So what about tonight's starter Jake Bennett? He just might be pitching for a postseason starting job over the next few weeks. If he does well and nobody steps up, the Sox could end up sending a rookie to the mound to start and do or die game in Yankee Stadium for the second year in a row.

And then there's Garrett Crochet, who won't be available to make a traditional start, but could be ramped up enough to give you a couple of innings out of the gate before you go bullpen game from there, mixing and matching the opponent with all your best arms and running their bench dry of platoon matchups by the late innings.

Those are just some of the factors on the table as we turn our eyes to the end of the month, but what does our OTM community think? Talk about this and whatever else you like, and as always, be good to one another!

articles.title: The Athletic releases long-awaited internal report on whether Dianna Russini’s relationship with Mike Vrabel affected reporting
articles.summary: Since April, The Athletic has been conducting a review of the work Dianna Russini produced while employed by the company and whether it was affected by her s...
articles.body:
Since April, The Athletic has been conducting a review of the work Dianna Russini produced while employed by the company and whether it was affected by her seeming years-long affair with NFL head coach Mike Vrabel.

The long-awaited report, reviewed this week by Awful Announcing, was published Thursday , providing the strongest insight yet into how Russini handled the initial revelations about her relationship with Vrabel — and to what extent that relationship may have affected her work covering the NFL.

Mike Semel, The Athletic's editorial director for standards and editorial quality, looked at 903 written stories, 204 episodes of the Scoop City podcast, and 77 videos contributed to by Russini during her tenure at the outlet. The report states that Semel also reviewed 25 external appearances Russini made, and interviewed 14 other Athletic staffers "who had worked most closely" with Russini.

In total, The Athletic determined that while its editorial standards were upheld, Russini's failure to disclose the conflict of interest with Vrabel stained some work.

"Russini's relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic's standards," the report reads. "Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed."

At least one story will be updated with an editor's note following the release of the report. One is a 2023 "What I'm Hearing" piece in which Russini reported on a Tennessee decision to attempt a two-point conversion. The blurb, Semel writes, "does not meet The Athletic's standards of attribution."

Semel recommends that The Athletic make its conflict-of-interest guidelines more "exact," clarify and "strongly enforce" its sourcing standards, and add a meeting with the standards editor to its typical onboarding procedures.

After the report was made public, Russini's former podcast, Scoop City, issued its first post on X in several months. It was a quote tweet of Russini's August 2025 interview with Vrabel that referenced the investigation and how Russini should have disclosed her relationship with Vrabel.

"Subsequent to the publication of this video, an Athletic inquiry into Dianna Russini's journalism determined that Russini should have disclosed the nature of her relationship with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel to her editors. She did not. It's now unclear whether The Athletic would have had the access to Vrabel for this interview had she disclosed their relationship," the post read.

The report also sheds light on the timeline of Russini's internal handling of the April 7 Page Six story containing photos of her and Vrabel at a resort in Sedona, Arizona.

Russini reportedly gave Athletic and New York Times management a heads-up that the Page Six story was coming the day it went out. The NFL insider acknowledged she had a close relationship with Vrabel, but stressed to her superiors that it was "strictly professional." At that time, per the report, Russini claimed there would be no further questionable pictures of her and Vrabel, "because she had never done anything inappropriate." She offered a similar statement to Page Six, though it proved untrue.

The report references a handful of instances of Russini writing about Vrabel in a manner "that in hindsight [is] awkward or even uncomfortable." One is from last season, in the lead-up to Vrabel's return to Tennessee .

"Vrabel is loud, direct and unapologetically himself," Russini wrote. "He's not for everyone."

But The Athletic reviewed other stories previewing that game and determined this was "the story line" of the game, and other outlets were similarly effusive about Vrabel's impact on both the Titans and his new team, the New England Patriots.

Russini resigned from The Athletic on April 14 , a week after the Page Six report. Later, additional photos surfaced showing her and Vrabel spending time together as far back as 2020, including one of them kissing .

The Athletic's initial defense of Russini to Page Six reportedly drew the ire of other staffers. It later launched an internal investigation , which morphed into Semel's review.

The pattern identified in Semel's report, and the timeline put forth by the tabloids, would also incriminate ESPN, where Russini worked from 2015-23. Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk previously highlighted a 2021 report from Russini on trade talks around Atlanta's Julio Jones, in which Russini overestimated the market for the star receiver in a way that could have benefited Tennessee, who ultimately acquired him.

Vrabel took time away from the Patriots during the NFL Draft and has said he went to counseling during the offseason.

Both are married with children. Neither has addressed the particular nature of their relationship.

articles.standfirst: Juan Fernando Quintero renuncia a la Selección Colombia: los motivos de su salida tras el Mundial 2026
articles.summary: Juan Fernando Quintero renuncia a la Selección Colombia: los motivos de su salida tras el Mundial 2026
articles.body: El fútbol colombiano vive el cierre de uno de sus capítulos más líricos y talentosos de la última década. Juan Fernando Quintero, el mediocampista antioqueño de 33 años y actual referente del Independiente Medellín, confirmó oficialmente su retiro definitivo de la Selección Colombia tras finalizar la participación del combinado patrio en la Copa del Mundo de 2026. La noticia, que venía gestándose entre rumores desde la eliminación en la cita orbital, fue ratificada por el propio 'Juanfer' en una emotiva entrevista concedida al programa Saque Largo de Win Sports, donde dejó en claro que su decisión se debe a un proceso de reflexión colectivo y al deseo de dar paso a las nuevas generaciones del balompié nacional. En sus declaraciones, Quintero confesó que el amargo trago que dejó la eliminación por penales ante Suiza en los octavos de final del Mundial 2026 fue el detonante definitivo para poner fin a su ciclo con la camiseta 'Tricolor'. "Yo dije que sí, que me hacía a un costado. Sentía que había llegado el momento, lo sentía así después de la frustración del Mundial y así se lo manifesté al cuerpo técnico y a los compañeros. Pienso mucho en colectivo. A veces uno piensa que es bueno salir o darse una oportunidad para que otro llegue", declaró el zurdo. Asimismo, Quintero despejó cualquier tipo de especulación sobre un distanciamiento con el estratega argentino Néstor Lorenzo o con el grupo de jugadores. Por el contrario, ratificó el profundo aprecio y respeto que siente por el cuerpo técnico: "Al profe lo quiero, lo aprecio, le deseo lo mejor y a mi país, es lo más hermoso que tenemos. Es un orgullo grandísimo ver las caras felices cuando te reconocen y te admiran". El legado de 'Juanfer' con la camiseta cafetera arrancó formalmente en 2012, cuando debutó bajo las órdenes de José Néstor Pékerman en un amistoso ante Camerún. Desde entonces, el talentoso creador integró una de las épocas más memorables del fútbol colombiano. Los números de 'Juanfer' con la Tricolor: Entre sus momentos más recordados en la memoria colectiva figura su antológico gol de tiro libre por debajo de la barrera contra Japón en el Mundial de Rusia 2018, además de convertirse en el primer futbolista colombiano en anotar en dos Mundiales consecutivos. Con la salida de Quintero, la Selección Colombia despide a uno de sus últimos exponentes del "10 clásico", un futbolista caracterizado por la pausa, la visión periférica y la capacidad de cambiar la dinámica de un partido con un solo zurdazo. Su decisión no solo responde a su propio desgaste físico y mental tras competir en el máximo nivel internacional, sino también a una postura consciente sobre la necesidad del recambio generacional en el mediocampo de la Selección. A partir de este momento, Juan Fernando Quintero enfocaría la totalidad de sus esfuerzos en la alta competencia a nivel de clubes con la camiseta de Independiente Medellín, cerrando así una brillante página en la historia de la Selección Colombia.

articles.body: Coco Gauff’s father Corey Gauff has defended Ben Shelton after an Instagram user criticized the American’s celebration following his second-round win at the 2026 US Open. Shelton beat Hubert Hurkacz 6-3, 5-7, 7-6(3), 7-5 at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Wednesday. After the win, Shelton celebrated with his team as the home crowd cheered. One fan called his reaction “way over the top,” and Corey responded, “Shut up.”Corey Gauff defends Ben Shelton after his US Open celebrationThe criticism appeared under a video posted by the official US Open Instagram account. The clip showed Shelton celebrating after a tense four-set battle with Hurkacz. The 23-year-old American roared, clenched his fists and went around to shake hands with members of his team.Shelton then met Hurkacz at the net and shared a respectful moment with the Polish player. Still, one fan was not impressed by the celebration and wrote, “Calm down dude… this guy is way over the top with his reactions.”Corey Gauff noticed the comment and replied with two simple words: “Shut up.” Corey is the father of American tennis star Coco Gauff, who is also competing at the US Open this year.Shelton’s reaction came after a match that had plenty of pressure. He took the opening set 6-3, but Hurkacz answered by winning the second 7-5. The third set went to a tiebreak, where Shelton moved ahead 7-3. Hurkacz stayed close in the fourth, but Shelton broke late and closed out the match 7-5.The official US Open website reported that Shelton was playing his first match against Hurkacz. It also noted that the American was wearing visible cupping marks on his left shoulder after the joint injury that forced him to retire from last year’s US Open.Ben Shelton praises fans after Hubert Hurkacz battleShelton’s celebration also made more sense when he spoke about the crowd after the match. The American said the match gave him useful experience and that he found several things in his game that he wants to carry into the next rounds.The win also kept Shelton’s US Open run moving after a demanding opening-round match against Tallon Griekspoor. He will now play Denis Shapovalov in the third round. The Canadian reached the round after beating Luca Van Assche. articles.title: Super League: Mark Percival to retire at end of season after 13-year career with St Helens
articles.summary: St Helens centre Mark Percival has announced he will retire at the end of the 2026 Super League season following a 14-season professional career with the club; round 26 of Super League begins on Thursday September 3 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Percival has made the decision in the wake of a recommendation to undergo a shoulder replacement at the end of the current campaign, bringing to an end a 14-season professional career spent entirely with the Saints after joining the club as a 14-year-old.

The 32-year-old Saints' legend was a part of five Super League title-winning Saints teams alongside winning four League Leaders' Shields, a Challenge Cup and the World Club Challenge.

"After a lot of thought, I have made the decision to retire from rugby league at the end of this season," Percival said in a statement on social media.

"Although this has been a very emotional decision, I know the time is right to put my health and my family first.

"Rugby league is a tough sport to which I have always given 100 per cent, this season it has heavily impacted my home life leading to medical advice to have my shoulder replaced at the end of this season.

"When I arrived at this club at 14 I never would have imagined I would be able to look back on such a fortunate career. I feel very lucky to have taken to the field with such a special group and very proud of the trophies and titles we have contributed to this great club's history.

"I will be eternally grateful for the memories both on and off the field and would like to thank my family, friends and staff that have supported me throughout the highs and lows of my career, I truly couldn't have done it without each of you."

St Helens chairman Eamonn McManus also paid tribute to Percival's career in a statement on the club's wesbite, adding: "Whilst it's sad that Percy is the latest, in quick succession after Tommy Makinson and Jonny Lomax, of a generation of truly great Saints players to announce their retirement, it also highlights and emphasises how fortunate we have been as a club to witness his and their careers.

"Percy's achievements are self-evident and all of his accolades richly deserved. But yet again, it is immense bravery and selflessness which distinguish him from other successful careers.

"On behalf of us all, thank you for the joy that you've brought to us all over the last 14 seasons, Percy, and the very best wishes to you and your family in your future lives together."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: Deadpool-Wolverine derby in the offing as Hugh Jackman targets Norwich City
articles.summary: After Deadpool actor Ryan Reynolds’s purchase of Wrexham, his Wolverine costar could land Championship rivals Norwich.
articles.body:
Hugh Jackman wants to join his fellow Hollywood star and friend Ryan Reynolds in owning part of a football club in the English leagues.

Jackman has long been a fan of Norwich, his mother’s home city in the east of England. The Wolverine star was asked in an interview broadcast on Thursday if he would like to “buy a bit” of the club, which is majority-owned by Mark Attanasio, the Milwaukee Brewers’ principal owner.

“I’m very, very interested in talking about it right now,” he told British broadcaster TalkSport while promoting his new movie, The Death of Robin Hood.

“You’re the first one to know that. There’s a little exclusive,” Jackman said when asked if he would “follow suit” with Reynolds, who put Wrexham on the global football and culture map after buying the club with Rob McElhenney in 2021.

Norwich and Wrexham are now rivals in the English second-tier Championship although Jackman’s team has the more illustrious history. Norwich last played in the Premier League four years ago and had perhaps its finest moment in 1993 when it eliminated German powerhouse Bayern Munich in the old UEFA Cup.

“Good on Ryan. You do your thing. I’m all about the Canaries,” Jackman said, using Norwich’s nickname, linked to the team’s distinctive yellow and green uniform.

Norwich and Wrexham both are expected to be contenders this season to earn promotion to the Premier League, the world’s most valuable club football competition.

“I think it’s an exciting team and it’s going to be an exciting year,” Jackman said, praising Norwich’s turnaround since hiring Belgian coach Philippe Clement in November.

St Helens centre and former England international Mark Percival will retire from rugby league at the end of the season.

The 32-year-old has spent his entire career with Saints and during that time won five Super League titles, four League Leaders' Shields, the Challenge Cup and the World Club Challenge.

He has made a total of 273 appearances for the club since making his debut in 2013 and has missed much of this season through injury - but he has been named in Saints' matchday squad , external to face Leigh Leopards this weekend.

"This has not been an easy decision, and there's a lot of emotion around it," Percival told the club website. , external

"I love this club so much, and I want to play. I want to be out there helping the team and to be with the fans, so not being able to do that has been difficult, and it makes this decision even harder.

"This is not a choice I've made overnight. It's always difficult when you have to step away, and knowing if it's the right decision can be hard too. Ultimately, I feel like this is going to be the right decision, even though my mind is telling me to play on; sadly, my body is telling me different.

"I'll be getting my shoulder replaced at the end of the year. It is what it is. Long-term it means I'll be able to pick my kids up and not deal with the symptoms I have this season, which is something I've been struggling with."

articles.body: Lewis Hamilton made a memorable entrance at the Italian Grand Prix on Thursday, arriving at Monza in his newly restored Ferrari F40 and immediately turning heads before the weekend’s action had even begun. The seven-time Formula 1 champion paired the iconic red Ferrari with a dark suit, tan coat and distinctive hat, creating a classic look that gave photographers plenty to capture. Hamilton’s choice of car was especially significant, as the F40 holds a deeply personal place in his story. The Ferrari legend was a childhood dream for the British driver, who recently revealed just how long he had wanted to own one. Now, with the beautifully restored F40 by his side, Hamilton brought together two of his greatest passions, Ferrari and some of the most iconic machinery ever produced by the Italian marque—making for an arrival perfectly suited to Monza.Lewis Hamilton shows off his Ferrari F40 at MonzaHamilton, 41, drove the classic Ferrari into the Monza circuit ahead of this weekend’s Italian Grand Prix. He later stopped for photographs beside the car, which has quickly become one of the most personal additions to his collection.His outfit also stood out. Hamilton wore a dark suit under a tan coat and added a quirky flat cap-style hat and sunglasses. The look came despite the warm Italian weather, but it matched the kind of bold fashion choices he often brings to Formula 1 paddocks.The F40 itself has an unusual story. Hamilton recently bought the car after it had spent more than 30 years sitting in a garage. Instead of simply taking it home, he sent it to Ferrari’s Maranello factory, where its restoration was handled by specialists.Hamilton explained on Instagram why the car means so much to him. He wrote, “My very own F40. This is the car of my dreams and has been for as long as I can remember.”He also said he had wanted one since he was a child and made sure an F40 was part of his first day at Ferrari in 2025.The exact value of Hamilton’s car has not been officially confirmed. While the original report described it as a £3 million Ferrari, recent reports have placed the restored F40’s value at more than £6 million. Its condition, history and rarity can make a major difference to its price.Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari F40 carries his famous number 44There is another detail that makes Hamilton’s F40 even more personal. The car carries the number 44, the racing number he has used throughout his Formula 1 career.For Hamilton, 44 goes back much further than his time in F1. He has previously explained that his father used an old go-kart with the number F44 when Hamilton was a child. That became the number he raced with before eventually choosing 44 as his permanent F1 number.The F40 also holds a special place in Ferrari history. The model was the final road car approved by Ferrari founder Enzo Ferrari and has become one of the company’s most famous classic cars.Hamilton’s arrival at Monza therefore brought together two things that have followed him for years: his love of Ferrari and the number that has been part of his racing story since childhood.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
Real Madrid ‌defender Raul Asencio has been cleared of charges ⁠related to ⁠sharing a sexually explicit video without the consent of the victims, including a minor, a court on the Spanish island of ⁠Gran Canaria said.

Prosecutors dropped the charges against Asencio on Thursday and reduced their sentencing requests for three other former Real Madrid ⁠youth players after the victims told the court they had forgiven the defendants.

The other three players, who were charged with recording and sharing sexual videos of two teenage women, one of ‌them underage, were sentenced to one year in prison. The sentences were suspended on condition that they commit no further offences during that period.

Asencio was accused of sharing the video but was not accused of filming it.

In an unrelated incident, Asencio was fined 14,400 euros ($16,800) and banned from driving for eight months after pleading guilty to driving under the influence of alcohol, ⁠another court said on Wednesday.

The 23-year-old centre-back was more than three times over the legal limit during the August 16 incident.

Earlier on Thursday, Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said the club had opened disciplinary proceedings against the player, but that Asencio ⁠would remain part of his plans while the matter was being resolved.

“He’s a model professional. When he was fit, no one trained as hard as him,” Mourinho told reporters.

“Now that he’s been injured for a few weeks, he’s the first to arrive and the last to leave [training]. But a Real Madrid player remains so 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 12 months a year.

“Everything you do ⁠outside your professional sphere still reflects ⁠on Real Madrid and continues to damage the reputation of a club whose standing must not be undermined.

“I’m not happy. Everyone makes mistakes, ‌but a series of mistakes is something different.”

Asencio has not played for the Spanish club this season because of ‌a hamstring injury that is expected to keep him out for a couple more weeks, Mourinho said.

articles.title: Anthony Richardson wins backup quarterback job for Colts, Keenan Allen stays mum on arrest
articles.summary: Receiver Keenan Allen and quarterback Anthony Richardson tried to keep Thursday's talk centered on football.  Both still sound content to be with the Indiana...
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Receiver Keenan Allen and quarterback Anthony Richardson tried to keep Thursday's talk centered on football. It wasn't easy in light of Allen's recent arrest on drunken driving charges or Richardson's offseason trade request.

Both still sound content to be with the Indianapolis Colts preparing for the Sept. 13 season opener against the Baltimore Ravens, even if they are playing very different roles.

Though coach Shane Steichen was essentially mum on Allen's situation, he wasted no time declaring Richardson the top backup to Daniel Jones for the second straight year. This time Richardson beat out Riley Leonard, who finished his rookie year by starting last season's finale.

"I thought Anthony played some better ball in the preseason," Steichen said. "I think both of them had pretty good camps. There are things they could both improve on, but I thought he (Richardson) did some good things in games."

Richardson's journey with the Colts has been an arduous one.

Indy took the athletic, strong-armed Florida star with the No. 4 overall draft pick in 2023, tabbing him as their future franchise quarterback. But a litany of injuries, concerns about his accuracy and the unforgettable image of taking himself briefly out of a game because he was "tired" prompted the Colts to sign Jones in free agency in 2025. That set up a rare training camp competition between Richardson and Jones.

When Jones was declared the winner, Richardson was relegated to backup duty before suffering a freak eye injury in October that ended his season.

Richardson made two trade requests and skipped the first weekend of Indy's offseason workouts, thinking a trade might happen on draft weekend. When it didn't, Richardson returned for the second week of offseason team activities and has largely sounded content to play his fourth and perhaps final season with the Colts.

"He'll be an Indianapolis Colt this year," general manager Chris Ballard said Tuesday when asked if he expects Richardson to be with the team this season.

Richardson also said he has not spoken with his agent about the trade request recently.

"When I reported back for OTAs, you know, I was here and told myself I was going to be here and prepare myself like I was going to be here for the start of the season," Richardson said. "So I'm still trying to do the same thing, prepare myself and get ready for Day 1."

Allen is scrambling to learn the playbook and his new teammates since signing with the Colts on Aug. 19, a move that reunited the six-time Pro Bowler with Steichen. The duo spent seven years together with the San Diego-Los Angeles Chargers.

Allen was arrested early Sunday morning, the first blip on an otherwise spotless record for the 14-year veteran who holds the Chargers career record for receptions. But he did not elaborate on what happened that night or the discussions he's had with Steichen and teammates since then.

"Because it's an ongoing legal matter, we're not going to discuss it," Allen said. "Like I said, just focusing on football and being a good team."

Steichen didn't add much, either, merely saying he expects Allen to play Week 1 — as Ballard said Tuesday.

"There's a legal situation going on right now, so I'm going to keep everything in house in that regard," Steichen said. "I've got a lot of respect for Keenan, and you know I had private conversations with him. Like I said, we'll keep that in house and keep that private."

Apparently, Allen continues to debate which jersey number to wear after giving away his preferred No. 13 to Laquon Treadwell. Allen was issued No. 10 when he arrived at training camp, and it seemed like that would be the choice — until he showed up with No. 11 for Thursday's workout.

The deadline for a final choice is looming, though.

"I tried it (No. 11) out today, I thought it was pretty sweet," Allen said. "Ten looked good, too, so we'll keep it going, probably figure it out before that (team picture next week)."

articles.title: Sussex's Crocombe takes second hat-trick in eight days
articles.summary: Sussex paceman Henry Crocombe takes a second hat-trick in consecutive games as Essex lose their last seven wickets for six runs.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Ambassador Cruise Line Ground, Chelmsford (day two)

Sussex 275: Leaning 60; Porter 4-44 & 90-4: Coles 29*; Harmer 2-19

Sussex (4 pts) lead Essex (3 pts) by 188 runs

Henry Crocombe claimed his second hat-trick in eight days, and third five-wicket haul of the season, to leave Essex's batting in total disarray on an incredible evening of tumbling wickets at Chelmsford.

The 24-year-old seamer, who leaves Sussex for Surrey at the end of the season, had never taken three wickets in successive balls before running through Somerset's tail at Hove last week.

For an encore he helped reduce Essex from 171-3 to 177 all out in the space of 26 balls, his five wickets coming in 14 deliveries without conceding a run. He finished with 5-39.

Essex had been progressing serenely after tea on the second day of the County Championship match when Charlie Allison became Crocombe's first victim after a tidy 56.

That wicket exposed the tender underbelly of Essex's batting and revived fears of a battle against relegation in the run-in to the Division One season.

The collapse gave Sussex an unexpected first-innings lead of 98 after they had taken their score to 275 in the morning, thanks largely to the re-engaged Ari Karvelas thrashing six fours in a breezy 38 from 44 balls.

However, they lost Tom Haines, Tom Clark, Charlie Tear and Oli Carter second time round in extending their advantage to 188 as 11 wickets fell after tea.

Karvelas was not finished when he was last man out in Sussex's first innings and, taking the new-ball, separated the Essex opening pair with an angled a delivery into Paul Walter's stumps. Tom Westley then had a rush of blood and, in attempting to heave Jack Carson over midwicket, was also bowled.

With the sun breaking through and a drying wind, the wicket flattened out and batting seemed to be becoming easier than on day one.

At that stage there was no hint of what was to come. Indeed, Essex reached three figures for two wickets down in 32 overs, 12 quicker than Sussex, the milestone reached with a reverse sweep for four by Allison off Carson.

Allison contributed 38 of a 58-run stand with Dean Elgar before James Coles found extravagant turn with his third ball to bowl Elgar.

Allison's eighth boundary, a drive off Tom Haines, took him to fifty from 60 balls, but he became bogged down, adding only six more from a further 26 balls before he was lbw playing around one from Crocombe.

Then came the carnage. Almost immediately Michael Pepper attempted to sweep Coles and went lbw. Then Crocombe took centre stage. Simon Harmer and Zaman Akhter were both trapped lbw to the first two balls of Crocombe's ninth over before Shane Snater played over the third and lost his leg stump.

Mitch Killeen had been recalled from a loan spell with Gloucestershire to replace Sam Cook, who was called up by England mid-match. Killeen lasted seven balls before he stepped back to try and cut Coles and was bowled. And it wasn't long before Jamie Porter became the sixth player to lose his stumps in the innings, wicket number five for a rampant Crocombe.

Essex took an hour to wrap up the last three Sussex wickets despite Cook removing Dom Goodman playing down the wrong line to the first ball of the morning. That only brought in Karvelas to help Sussex add 62 runs and claim a batting point.

Karvelas was playing a first-class game for the first time in a year after being released by the club. The South African seamer has since worked as a coach in the Sussex academy and been re-signed on a short-term contract to cover injuries and England call-ups.

Jack Leaning put on 36 for the ninth wicket with Karvelas before falling to another catch behind off Akhter for a 110-ball 60. Karvelas was finally out when he edged Porter to give Pepper a fifth catch in the innings and Porter his 600th first-class wicket in figures of 4-44.

articles.title: Yankees at Padres: 5 things to watch and series predictions | Sept. 4-6
articles.summary: Here are five things to watch and predictions as the Yankees travel to San Diego to take on the Padres in a three-game series starting Friday...
articles.body:
Here are five things to watch and predictions as the Yankees travel to San Diego to take on the Padres in a three-game series starting Friday...

George Lombard Jr. has missed four straight games after injuring his right knee on a swing in the second of last Saturday's doubleheader with the Red Sox.

The Yankees maintain it's a day-to-day situation, and there's an expectation that the shortstop will return to the lineup when the series starts up on Friday, and New York could use the youngster.

Jose Caballero has valiantly started at shortstop, but he has not had a good road trip. He went 1-for-12 with seven strikeouts -- including two errors -- in the three-game series with the Angels. While Lombard wasn't hitting well when he got injured, 5-for-24 in his last seven games, he continued to put professional at-bats and get on base regularly.

And after Lombard's error streak came to an end, that elite defense began to show up again, which the Yankees can always use.

Since the injury to Fernando Cruz , the Yankees have had to use different pitchers to fill the bullpen.

John Schreiber, Michael Fulmer and Luis Gil are the new faces in the 'pen and vying to earn Aaron Boone 's trust and make their way onto the postseason roster.

All three have been solid so far, and with Clarke Schmidt 's return imminent -- and also pitching for a spot in the bullpen -- this weekend will be another testing ground for these three arms.

Trent Grisham has struggled of late on both sides of the ball. So much so that Boone benched the veteran and used Spencer Jones in center field in the series finale with the Angels.

Over his last seven games, Grisham is 2-for-22 while Jones is 6-for-18 with two home runs.

Jones looked competent in center field on Wednesday and is athletic enough to handle the position, but how often will Boone have the rookie start instead of Grisham? They are both left-handers, so the starting pitcher may determine who plays.

San Diego will deploy Walker Buehler (RHP), Robbie Ray (LHP) and Michael King (RHP) this weekend. That could mean Grisham gets the start against the right-handers with Jones -- who is hitting southpaws better than Grisham -- to start the middle game. But we'll just have to wait and see how Boone handles the playing time.

Elmer Rodrigue z's spot in the rotation is for Sunday's series finale and the Yankees have yet to announce who will start that game.

Rodriguez, after the best start of his big league career, had arguably his worst. Monday against the Angels, Rodriguez allowed four runs in 3.2 innings and set the Yankees back for the rest of the series with all the relievers they had to use in the opener.

Will Boone give the ball to Rodriguez one more time? Ryan Weathers could be activated for the following series, so this could be the last chance to make an impression for the rookie. Or, with the off day Monday, the Yankees could go with a bullpen game and activate Weathers for the home series against the Rockies.

The Yankees enter play Thursday 3.5 games behind the Rays for the AL East crown. With a major four-game series with Tampa later this month, the Yankees hope to draw closer this weekend.

Of course, the Padres are in the midst of a playoff race of their own. They enter play 0.5 games out of the final wild card spot and every game is dire for them.

Bellinger has been hot since coming off the IL. He's 12-for-29 over his last seven, including going 8-for-14 against the Angels.

Which Yankees pitcher will have the best start?

Fried struggled in his first start off the IL, unable to get out of the fourth inning, but he'll find his way this weekend.

Which Padres player will be a thorn in the Yankees' side?

The shortstop has turned his season around after a slow start and that continues this weekend.

articles.title: Dayton Stivers football season back on, changing Cincinnati schedules
articles.summary: Just one day after cancelling the remainder of the 2026 football season, Dayton Stivers' season is back on. Here's what that means for Cincy teams.
articles.body:
Dayton Stivers School for the Arts abruptly changed course and will resume its 2026 football season.

After announcing the cancellation of Stivers's season on Monday, Aug. 31, Dayton Public Schools reversed the decision on Wednesday, Sept. 2, following a meeting with football parents.

"After listening to your concerns and suggestions, we've decided to move forward with the football season at Stivers School for the Arts. Thank you for your thoughtful, passionate comments in defense of your children and extracurricular activities," Superintendant David Lawrence said in a statement.

The season was initially cancelled due to low participation numbers and injuries. DPS will continue to monitor the situation to address player safety concerns.

Setting the scene - Week 2 football fans, bands, cheerleaders | Photos

Four Greater Cincinnati Schools were scheduled to play Stivers later this season. New Miami already replaced Stivers on the schedule with Preble Shawnee, playing later today, Sept. 3. Other future opponents included Shroder (Sept. 24), Norwood (Oct. 2), and Summit Country Day (Oct. 9).

Norwood athletic director Chuck Richardson III announced the school would honor the game against Stivers on Oct. 2.

Summit Country Day athletic director Greg Dennis confirmed that the team will still replace Stivers with a second matchup against Miami Valley Christian Academy on Oct. 9.

Shroder had not yet found a replacement game as of Sept. 2, and did not immediately respond to an inquiry about their updated scheduling plans.

Stivers competes in OHSAA Division V and is in just its second season after a being revived from a 40-year absence. The team went 2-8 last season, forfeiting one game. In the first game of the 2026 season Stivers lost to Gamble Montessori, 50-6. A week two game against Dunbar was cancelled.

One factor influencing DPS's decision to revive the season was the inability for Stivers players to continue the season with other Dayton Schools. Unlike Cincinnati's Lockland, which cancelled its season in early August, Stivers players were not eligible to play for neighboring schools. Since the season has already begun, OHSAA bylaw 4-1-4 considered the school to have sponsored the sport.

Families of the Stivers football team are expected to receive written plans for the remainder of the season sometime on Sept. 3.

"You've just got to learn from it and let's hope they can improve and do better in the bigger games," Wark told BBC Radio Suffolk.

"With spending, money-wise they have done enough but you don't know how good the players are going to be yet. They have spent loads of money but I just hope they all come together and it works for us."

Friday night's home game against Liverpool could see a debut handed to new striker signing Zian Flemming, who was signed for £20m from Burnley this week.

The 28-year-old scored 11 times last season in the Premier League for the Clarets, who were relegated. He has netted three in the first four games of the Championship campaign.

articles.title: SEC files lawsuit against LSU, Lane Kiffin over player eligiblity
articles.summary: The SEC has filed a lawsuit against officials at LSU, including football coach Lane Kiffin, amid plans for the school to field players from the NFL.
articles.body:
The SEC has filed a lawsuit against LSU and Lane Kiffin that asks for an injunction overruling a recent decision in a Louisiana court that allowed more than a dozen former college athletes to return to college despite concluding their eligibility this past season.

Filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Alabama, the SEC lawsuit also names LSU President Wade Rouse and athletics director Verge Ausberry.

LSU and Kiffin have come under intense scrutiny after the latter welcomed into his program former athletes who had already participated in NFL training camps, including potentially key additions who played for Kiffin last season when he was the coach at Mississippi.

"Defendants waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes to play football for LSU during the 2026-27 season, including players who had signed NFL contracts with the Cleveland Browns , New Orleans Saints , and Tampa Bay Buccaneers ," the SEC said in the suit.

On Aug. 19, a Louisiana judge issued a temporary restraining order allowing former athletes who had concluded four seasons of eligibility during the past academic year to return to the NCAA level following the organization's recent implementation of a five-for-five eligibility rule.

That order named names the SEC and Commissioner Greg Sankey as defendants and precluded them from enforcing a new conference policy that would deal significant penalties on schools that field players with professional experience.

Under the NCAA's new eligibility rule, college athletes will have five years to complete five seasons of eligibility, with the clock starting on the day of their enrollment in college or the start of the 19th birthday, whichever comes first.

The Louisiana ruling allowed athletes who enrolled as part of the high school class of 2022 to gain a fifth year of eligibility.

On August 25, SEC presidents, chancellors and athletics directors unanimously adopted a new policy that made it a violation of conference bylaws to sign or roster a player with professional experience.
