articles.title: Predictions: Michigan State football vs. Toledo
articles.summary: Angelique Chengelis, Connor Earegood, John Niyo, and Bob Wojnowski of The Detroit News predict the outcome of Friday's Michigan State-Toledo game.
articles.body:
Angelique Chengelis, Connor Earegood, John Niyo, and Bob Wojnowski of The Detroit News predict the outcome of Friday's Michigan State-Toledo game at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing (8 p.m., FS1/760) .

▶ Angelique S. Chengelis: Michigan State and Toledo have new head coaches this year, Pat Fitzgerald at MSU and Mike Jacobs with the Rockets , and this is an important first game for both coaches who want to set the tone for the season. Fitzgerald, without coaching a game, already feels like the right fit at MSU and that will be evident with this season opener as the Spartans play with a toughness that mirrors their head coach. Toledo had a top-rated defense last year, but much has changed and MSU sophomore quarterback Alessio Milivojevic, who has continued to make strides since last season when he played in nine games, should come out of the gate well. Pick: Michigan State, 24-10

▶ Connor Earegood : Pat Fitzgerald joked Monday that he'd rather open against his old Loyola Academy high school team than a Toledo team that is usually a MAC contender — then a big win over Cathedral gave Loyola a national ranking. Irish wit aside, there will probably be some emotion for Fitzgerald's return to the collegiate sidelines, and for the debuts of some key players in green and white. There's upset potential for a Toledo group built from pieces coach Mike Jacobs took from his old Mercer squad, including FCS defensive player of the year Andrew Zock. But Michigan State has plenty of talent, and plenty of coaching, to get the job done. Expect running back Cam Edwards to make a strong introduction. The bold prediction: don't be surprised if this defense gets a couple takeaways. Pick: Michigan State, 27-10

▶ John Niyo: Toledo's a perennial winner in the MAC, but the Rockets are at a different stage to start this season. And while everyone here is focused on the start of a new era at Michigan State, the change has been even more dramatic for the Spartans ' Week 1 opponent. Toledo may have just one returning starter on either side of the ball, not including the FCS transfers that followed Mike Jacobs from Mercer. Expect Michigan State's refurbished offensive line to assert itself in this one and give Pat Fitzgerald some early momentum on the field. Pick: Michigan State, 31-17

▶ Bob Wojnowski: We know Pat Fitzgerald will have his first MSU team emotionally ready under the lights. Beyond that, lots of unknowns. We don't know how quickly he's able to shore up the offensive and defensive lines, because that's where it begins for the Spartans. Transfer back Cam Edwards has generated considerable buzz, and returning quarterback Alessio Milivojevic shows promise. But MSU doesn't have an abundance of skill players, which will make this game a grind. Toledo also has a new coach, Mike Jacobs, who brought key players from his successful stint at Mercer. The Rockets are MAC contenders and always dangerous, but have an inexperienced quarterback in John Alan Richter and not enough firepower to pull the upset. Pick: Michigan State, 27-16

The Arizona Cardinals locked up one of their young wide receivers to an extension on Thursday.

According to NFL insiders Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter , the Cardinals have signed wideout Michael Wilson to a three-year, $75 million extension with a maximum value of $78 million.

The deal also includes $47 million in guaranteed compensation.

Wilson had the best season of his career in 2025, finishing with 78 receptions for 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns. He established himself as one of the Cardinals' best playmakers, and there's still room for him to grow.

In three seasons, Wilson has compiled 163 receptions for 2,119 yards and 14 touchdowns. He was selected by the Cardinals in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Stanford.

The Cardinals likely wanted this done before the start of the 2026 season so they could focus on other things, including prepping for the Los Angeles Chargers on Sept. 13. It will be the Cardinals' first regular-season game of the year.

articles.title: Guarino focused on the process as West Ham United look to build in 2026/2027
articles.summary: West Ham United head coach Rita Guarino says that she is focused on the process as her side look to build on the foundations that were put down in the second...
articles.body:
West Ham United head coach Rita Guarino says that she is focused on the process as her side look to build on the foundations that were put down in the second half of last season.

The Hammers finished the 2025/2026 campaign in 10th position in the Barclays Women's Super League table. The East Londoners struggled in the first half of the season but Guarino's arrival in December sparked an upturn in results.

When speaking to the media ahead of this weekend's opening Barclays Women's Super League fixture at Tottenham Hotspur, Guarino said that the focus is on the process and performing to a high level this season.

"We are a good team, we have lost some players and have signed some new players," Guarino said. "It's not about what we want to achieve in the mid-term, it's about the way that we want to improve this team during this season. It's about performing the best that we can and playing in the best way possible.

"It's important to stay in the league and I know that this team can compete with everyone. When you can compete, it means that you can perform at the highest level possible. For me, the focus with the team is on the process."

West Ham United have enjoyed a fruitful summer in the transfer market with several experienced players making the move to The Chigwell Construction Stadium. Guarino is happy with the club's transfer business.

She said "We have new players in the squad and I'm very happy from a personal point of view because they share the values of the club and philosophy of the team.

"I am very happy that they have easily integrated into the team alongside those players who have been here for many years. The feeling and connection with the other players has been very good , so I am very happy about this."

A derby against Spurs is never an easy assignment and Guarino provided her thoughts on the opposition.

She said "I think they are a very good team, a very competitive team. I think they have the ambition to be at the very top end of the table. They have a solid identity, they play very good football. They have some new players from last year and a large squad."

West Ham United's Barclays Women's Super League fixture at Tottenham Hotspur kicks-off at 12pm on Sunday afternoon.

articles.title: Israeli athletes removed from race amid 'safety concerns'
articles.summary: Four Israeli triathletes had been listed on a provisional entry list for the men's elite race in Derry, but were withdrawn after organisers raised concerns a...
articles.body:
A number of Israeli triathletes set to compete in Londonderry have been withdrawn from the race after organisers raised concerns about their participation.

The sport's governing body, World Triathlon, confirmed on Thursday it had been asked by the Israeli National Federation to "remove all the Israeli athletes entered" from Saturday's Europe Triathlon Cup.

The North West Triathlon Club (NWTC), who are organising the race, earlier said they could not support the Israeli athletes taking part.

The club added that it had concerns about "athlete and public safety" had the Israeli athletes competed on Saturday.

The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) told BBC News NI it had "become aware of potential protest activity in relation to the event".

Four Israeli triathletes had been listed on a provisional entry list for the men's elite race in Derry.

World Triathlon said it had removed the Israeli competitors with "immediate effect" following the request from the Israeli federation.

Earlier the NWTC said it had raised a number of concerns with both Triathlon Ireland and Europe Triathlon after it said it had become aware of the Israeli athletes participation.

It said it had "made clear in the strongest possible terms that it could not support their (the Israel athletes) participation in the circumstances."

That position, NWTC said, is based on its club values, the values of its members and "on the very real concerns being raised around athlete and public safety, the potential for serious disruption and the wider risk to an event involving hundreds of competitors from Ireland and across the world."

"This is not a position directed at anyone because of their religion or ethnicity, nor is it hostility towards an individual simply because they were born in Israel," NWTC said.

The race organisers added: "It is a position concerning representation of the State of Israel in international sport and the attempt to present normality on the international sporting stage while Palestinians continue to suffer."

"NWTC believed it had a responsibility to speak clearly and urgently when the safety of athletes, spectators, volunteers and the wider public - and potentially the ability of the event itself to proceed - could be placed at risk."

NWTC said international registration for the event has been handled by World Triathlon and as such it had "no involvement whatsoever in accepting or approving these international entries."

In a statement, Triathlon Ireland confirmed the start list for Saturday's race "does not include any athletes representing Israel."

"The selection and confirmation of athletes for Europe Triathlon Cup competition is managed by Europe Triathlon, under World Triathlon rules. It is not possible to comment on the circumstances or decisions relating to individual athletes," it said.

Triathlon Ireland added: "Preparations for Saturday's event are continuing as planned."

In a statement on social media, the Derry Anti War Coalition said it is "delighted that the triathletes from Israel will no longer be participating in the City of Derry Triathlon."

Staging an elite triathlon in the city is widely regarded as a coup for race organisers with many of the world's best triathletes set to take part.

Earlier this year, Ireland's most successful triathlete Aileen Reid said the Derry event – taking place three weeks before the World Triathlon Championship Finals in the Spanish city of Pontevedra - is well timed to attract a high-end field of competitors.

Derry City and Strabane District Council (DCSDC) said the event was not organised by it, but that Triathlon Ireland had secured funding through the National Event Fund to deliver it.

A spokesperson said: "We were made aware on Wednesday evening of concerns regarding a small number of entrants taking part, and are aware of the subsequent statement from the North West Triathlon Club issued today.

"We would like to take this opportunity to highlight Council's ongoing support for the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement which is promoted on our platforms regularly in line with the wider global campaign of solidarity with the Palestinian people."

articles.title: Did CJ Carr accidentally leak Notre Dame’s starting offensive line?
articles.summary: Notre Dame’s starting quarterback CJ Carr spoke with reporters on Wednesday, and he may have hinted at who the Irish’s starting offensive line will be.
articles.body:
On Wednesday evening, multiple Notre Dame coaches and players spoke with the media , and starting quarterback CJ Car may have given out some information that was supposed to be a secret until Sunday.

The star redshirt sophomore was speaking about the experience that his offensive line has as Mike Berardino posted on social media , with him mentioning Anthonie Knapp, Ashton Craig, Guerby Lambert, Will Black and Styles Prescod. When the Irish released their depth chart for Wisconsin , Prescod and Sullivan Absher were bracketed with the or designation, but Carr may have leaked the five who will join him for the first snaps of the season.

It has been quite the rise for Prescod, as many had him after an afterthought heading into this season, but he has turned the corner. The Irish have one of the best player development programs in the country, and it shouldn't come as a surprise that one of the lower ranked prospects has made a move towards a starting position.

The Badgers don't have elite talent upfront like other teams on the schedule, and it makes plenty of sense for Notre Dame to rotate players in during the first game to see how they work as a unit. Expect to see all six of these offensive lineman on the field Sunday night.

articles.title: Huddersfield sign former Colchester striker Tovide
articles.summary: Huddersfield Town sign former Colchester United forward Samson Tovide on a three-year deal following his departure from the Essex club.
articles.body:
Huddersfield Town have signed former Colchester United forward Samson Tovide on a three-year deal.

Colchester had been in contract discussions with Tovide following the conclusion of last season.

He made 151 appearances in all competitions for the Essex club after coming through their academy and scored 21 goals prior to his exit earlier this summer.

"This has been an important summer for me, and I've had a choice to make in which team I thought would be right to take the next step with in my career and develop my game," he told the Huddersfield website.

"In every conversation with the club, it gave me huge confidence about coming to Huddersfield Town, and I feel very blessed and honoured to sign for such a big club."

articles.title: Inside the Leonard Williams deal
articles.summary: The Seahawks recently signed defensive tackle Leonard to a new deal.
articles.body:
The Seahawks recently signed defensive tackle Leonard to a new deal.

We've gotten the details of the three-year, $90 million extension.

Here they are, per a source with knowledge of the terms:

1. Signing bonus: $22 million. (The first $10 million is due within 15 days of signing. The next $6 million is due by September 15, 2026. The final $6 million is due by April 15, 2027.)

2. 2026 base salary: $3.8 million, fully guaranteed.

3. 2026 per-game roster bonus: $850,000 total, fully guaranteed (but must be earned).

4. 2026 offseason workout bonus: $250,000.

5. 2027 option bonus: $10 million, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed on the fifth day of the 2027 waiver period.

6. 2027 base salary: $10.73 million, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed on the fifth day of the 2027 waiver period.

7. 2027 per-game active roster bonus: $1.02 million total, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed on the fifth day of the 2027 waiver period (but must be earned).

8. 2028 offseason workout bonus: $250,000.

9. 2028 option bonus: $10 million, $5.35 million of which is guaranteed for injury at signing, and fully guaranteed on the fifth day of the waiver period.

11. 2028 per-game active roster bonus: $1.02 million total.

12. 2029 offseason workout bonus: $250,000.

14. 2029 per-game active roster bonus: $1.02 million total.

The contract includes a $2 million 2028 escalator if Williams is a first- or second-team All-Pro in 2027, and a $2 million 2028 incentive if he is a first- or second-team All-Pro in 2028. If achieved, these amounts reduce his 2029 pay by up to $4 million.

As a practical matter, the four-year deal is guaranteed for the first two, at a total payout of $48.65 million. After that, it's year to year.

The final year has total compensation of $34 million, which gets the three-year, new-money average up to $30 million annually but likely will go away, one way or the other. That makes it a two-year extension with an average value of $28 million in new money.

articles.title: Houston Astros' Josh Hader earns American League accolade for August after scoreless month
articles.summary: Josh Hader picked up his ninth reliever of the month award, the second-most all-time, after not allowing a run in August.
articles.body:
Houston Astros closer Josh Hader was named the American League reliever of the month for August, the league announced Thursday.

Hader did not allow a run in 13 appearances in August. Over 14 ⅓ innings, the left-hander allowed four hits, issued one walk and struck out 15 of 48 batters faced. He converted all seven of his save attempts.

The monthly honor is the ninth of Hader's career. That is second-most for any reliever, after Edwin Díaz 's 10 recognitions, since the reliever of the month award was introduced in 2005, per the league.

After missing the season's first two months on the injured list, Hader entered Thursday with a 0.72 ERA in 38 outings. He was 22-for-22 in save chances with a .111 opponents batting average and 35.8% strikeout rate.

Hader, who is in the third season of a five-year, $95 million deal, made his 500th career appearance last month. He is one of three pitchers to be named reliever of the month with three different teams - also receiving the recognition with the Brewers and Padres - along with Aroldis Chapman and Craig Kimbrel .

articles.title: Richarlison left out of Tottenham’s Premier League squad
articles.summary: Richarlison said ‘never again will anyone decide my future for me’ but could soon find himself leaving the club
articles.body:
Tottenham have omitted Richarlison from their Premier League squad, with the striker reportedly not part of their plans for the season.

The decision comes after proposed talks over Richarlison returning to Everton broke down, resulting in the forward posting an emotional statement on social media, writing that "never again will anyone decide my future for me".

However, the Tottenham hierarchy seem to have decided his future is not at the club, with the transfer windows for Turkish and Saudi Arabian clubs still open and a move away likely.

The 29-year-old was informed of the decision to omit him from the squad before Tuesday's Premier League transfer window deadline amid reports that Turkish side Trabzonspor intend to make a formal approach for him.

Spurs manager Roberto de Zerbi said the Brazilian was left out of the squad for their 2-0 defeat to Newcastle because "too many times he asked to leave".

The club entered talks with Everton on Sunday night over the possibility of Richarlison returning to his former club, while also discussing a move for Toffees star Iliman Ndiaye, who ultimately signed for Manchester City.

Richarlison responded with an emotional post on social media, writing: "After everything I've been through in the last few years, I've decided that never again will anyone decide my future for me.

"I went through a lot of bad things, and almost all of them happened because decisions were made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I've been through far worse, believe me.

"I've always made it clear, every time I had the chance, that leaving for another club would only happen if it was also good for the club. If it wasn't, I would never accept it. Just like I didn't accept it when everything was going badly and they needed me.

"I stayed and gave everything. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect I've always shown Spurs and everyone who worked with me during this period. Just don't try to decide for me.

"If they reach an agreement between Spurs and Everton, I will return to my beloved club. My intention was to go back to the place where I was very happy, yes, but the negotiations happened only in the way certain people wanted, and it will no longer be like that.

"Despite all this turmoil, I am under contract at Spurs and will remain at the club's disposal."

Richarlison joined Tottenham from Everton in 2022.

articles.title: Will Levis, Jack Plummer worked out for Jets on Thursday
articles.summary: The Jets are looking at adding another quarterback to their broader roster.
articles.body:
The Jets are looking at adding another quarterback to their broader roster.

According to Zack Rosenblatt of TheAthletic.com, New York worked out Will Levis and Jack Plummer for a spot on the practice squad on Thursday.

Levis, a second-round pick in 2023, was waived by the Titans as part of their roster cuts over the weekend and went unclaimed. While he missed the 2025 season due to injury, he started 21 games for Tennessee from 2023-2024, completing 61.0 percent of his passes for 3,899 yards with 21 touchdowns and 16 interceptions.

Plummer is the UFL's reigning MVP, having won it for his season with the Orlando Storm. He led the UFL with 2,188 passing yards while tossing 17 touchdowns with just one interception in 10 games. He previously spent time with the Panthers and worked out for the 49ers and Dolphins this summer.

New York currently has just rookie Cade Klubnik on its 53-man roster at quarterback behind starter Geno Smith. Veteran Bailey Zappe is on the team's practice squad.

articles.title: Adams century put Hants in One-Day Cup knockouts
articles.summary: Hampshire qualify for the One-Day Cup knockout stages, while Somerset, Warwickshire and Lancashire stay in contention after also winning.
articles.body:
A superb all-round performance from captain Georgia Adams was the foundation of the win that secured Hampshire a place in the knockout stages of the One-Day Cup.

Adams took 2-26 with the ball as Durham were restricted to 200-9 before she hit an unbeaten 106 to lead her side home by nine wickets with more 12 overs to spare at Chester-le-Street.

The result sees Hampshire join The Blaze in qualifying but the third and final spot remains tight.

Warwickshire jumped into third thanks to cruising to a seven-wicket triumph over bottom side Essex at Edgbaston. That put them one point clear of Somerset, who came through a remarkable five-run win over Yorkshire at Headingley.

Meanwhile defending champions Lancashire continued their late push with a fourth straight win as they overcame Surrey by 10 runs on the DLS method at Farington.

Last year's runners-up Hampshire had seen their progress to a guaranteed top-three finish held up by losing to Lancashire, but they were back on form against Durham .

The hosts opted to bat, but Adams and fellow spinner Amanda-Jane Wellington took a combined 5-56 from 20 overs to restrict them.

Durham were 129-8 and then 158-9 before an unbroken last-wicket stand of 42 in four overs between young Australian Eleanor Larosa, who finished on 51 off 36 balls and Katie Levick (12) pushed the total to 200-9.

But Adams made short work of the chase, putting on 86 with fellow opener Ella McCaughan (31) and then 115 with Abi Norgrove, who was 59 not out.

The captain finished on 106 off as many balls as the five points were collected with 12.3 overs in hand.

Warwickshire took full advantage of playing struggling Essex with a maximum point triumph.

The visitors batted first and were salvaged by a 75-run sixth-wicket partnership from 115-5 between Liberty Heap, who top scored with 52 and Sophia Smale, 42.

But 4-42 from Phoebe Brett and 3-26 from another spinner in Hannah Baker saw Essex eventually all out for 202 in the 45th over.

In reply, the Bears fell to 86-3, but captain Katie George and Abi Freeborn came together to take hold of the game.

They put on 122 at more than a run-a-ball with Freeborn on 64 and George, who ended the game with a six, on 72 as victory was wrapped up with 81 balls to spare with the Warwickshire skipper delivering a fourth half-century of the competition to go with one century.

Victory from jaws of defeat for Somerset

Somerset began the day in third and slumped to 21-5 after Yorkshire asked them to bat with Hannah Rainey and Jess Woolston ripping through the order.

Jess Hazell battled to 33, and others chipped in as they eventually scrambled their way to 130 before being bowled out in the 39th over.

Yorkshire quickly slipped to 22-3 but 29 from Erin Thomas and then Ami Campbell with 35 looked to have got them over the line at 121-5 and with only 10 needed to win.

But Campbell was run out, sparking an incredible collapse of five wickets for four runs with four wickets falling on 121 before Rainey was bowled by Chloe Skelton, who took 4-28, to cap the incredible turnaround.

After losing seven of their opening nine games, Lancashire are gathering some late momentum to remain in the hunt.

Tilly Kesteven hit a career-best 85, batting at number three, to anchor her side's total of 234-9 off their 50 overs as they played their first competitive match at the club's new second home at Farington.

Surrey were going well at 85-2 but lost two wickets for two runs including Phoebe Franklin for 43 to tilt things back in the Red Rose's favour.

However, with rain threatening, the match was decided in what turned out to be the final over.

The fall of wicketkeeper Jemina Spence, lbw to Fi Morris for 41, put the DLS score back in Lancashire's favour and one ball later, the umpires took the players off for rain with them not to return.
